newsitem.title: USA: Simpson child custody case gets underway.
newsitem.headline: Simpson child custody case gets underway.

text.p: The child custody battle pitting O.J. Simpson against the parents of his slain ex-wife began here Tuesday, according to a court spokeswoman.
A smiling Simpson was greeted by dozens of reporters and camera crews outside the courthouse as he arrived at the closed-door custody hearing in Orange County family court.

Nicole Brown Simpson's parents, Louis and Juditha Brown, have had temporary guardianship of Simpson's daughter, Sydney, 11, and his son, Justin, 8, since just after their mother's murder in June 1994.
Simpson was acquitted in October 1995, in the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend, Ronald Goldman.
The former professional athlete, a member of the professional football Hall of Fame, beat his wife during their marriage, according to court records.
Simpson is now on trial in civil court facing a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the victims' families.

Simpson turned the children over to the Browns in June 1994, after he was arrested on murder charges. The children have had weekend visits with Simpson since his acquittal, but he is challenging the Browns to regain full custody.

Simpson contends that since he is the biological father, he should get sole custody. He is reportedly concerned that living with the Browns, who are white, the children are not learning enough about their black heritage.
Attorneys for the Browns contend that Simpson is unfit to raise the children.
